questions.question: If a wooden chair, a metal coin, and a plastic cup are left in a sealed room at 20ºC for several days, what can we say about their temperatures?
options: The metal coin will be colder than the wooden chair and plastic cup.
The wooden chair will be warmer than the plastic cup and metal coin.
All three objects will have reached the same temperature of 20ºC.
Only the plastic cup will reach 20ºC while the others stay at different temperatures.

questions.question: What happens to the spacing between particles when a liquid is heated?
options: The separation between the particles increases.
The separation between the particles decreases.
The particles get closer together while becoming smaller.
The spacing remains completely unchanged.

questions.question: Why does the metal lid of a glass jar often become easier to unscrew after being placed under hot running water?
options: The hot water causes the metal lid to expand.
The hot water causes the glass jar to contract.
The hot water makes the metal particles shrink.
The hot water dissolves the glue holding the lid.

questions.question: Under which condition will a cup of boiling hot tea (at 95ºC) transfer energy to the surrounding air at the fastest initial rate?
options: When placed in a warm room at 30ºC.
When placed in a comfortable room at 20ºC.
When placed in a cool room at 15ºC.
When placed in a freezing cold room at 2ºC.

questions.question: Why do different substances of the same mass require different amounts of heating to reach the exact same target temperature?
options: Different substances have different properties, requiring different amounts of heating to reach the same temperature.
Some substances have particles that never move or vibrate.
All substances require the exact same amount of heating regardless of their composition.
Only liquids require heating, while solids reach temperatures automatically.

questions.question: If Substance X has a higher specific heat capacity than Substance Y, what does this tell us about 1 kg of each substance at 50ºC?
options: Substance X has more energy in its thermal store than Substance Y.
Substance Y has more energy in its thermal store than Substance X.
Both substances have the exact same amount of energy in their thermal stores.
Substance X has heavier particles than Substance Y.

questions.question: In which states of matter do the particles move or vibrate in random directions?
options: Only in gases.
Only in liquids and gases.
In solids, liquids, and gases.
Only in solids.

questions.question: Consider two identical copper blocks: Block A is at 80ºC and Block B is at 30ºC. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block B, because its particles are more tightly packed.
Block A, because it is at a higher temperature.
Both blocks have the same energy because they are identical in size.
Neither block has any energy because they are both solids.

questions.question: Two buckets contain pure water at exactly 40ºC. Bucket 1 contains 10 litres of water and Bucket 2 contains 1 litre of water. Which bucket contains more thermal energy?
options: Bucket 1, because it has more particles.
Bucket 2, because the particles are more compressed.
Both have the same thermal energy because they are at the same temperature.
Neither has thermal energy because 40ºC is too cold.

questions.question: How must you position your eye to get an accurate reading when using a glass thermometer?
options: Look down at the thermometer from directly above.
Look up at the thermometer from directly below.
Ensure your eye is level with the top of the coloured liquid.
Hold the thermometer at an angle of 45 degrees to your face.

questions.question: What are the melting point of pure ice and the boiling point of pure water under standard conditions?
options: Melts at 10ºC, boils at 90ºC.
Melts at 0ºC, boils at 100ºC.
Melts at -5ºC, boils at 105ºC.
Melts at 100ºC, boils at 0ºC.

questions.question: If you mix 5 litres of boiling hot water with 1 litre of ice-cold water, what will the final temperature be closest to?
options: Exactly halfway between the hot and cold temperatures.
It will be closer to the temperature of the cold water.
It will be closer to the temperature of the hot water.
It will boil instantly and evaporate.

questions.question: What happens to the particles when a hot metal bolt is placed into a beaker of cold water?
options: Water particles move more quickly, and metal particles move more slowly.
Water particles move more slowly, and metal particles move more quickly.
Both water and metal particles begin to move more slowly.
Both water and metal particles begin to move more quickly.

questions.question: When one end of a thermal insulator is heated, what happens to the temperature along the rest of the insulator?
options: It increases very rapidly.
It increases very slowly.
It drops immediately to absolute zero.
It stays completely at 0ºC forever.

questions.question: Why does a fleece jacket containing trapped pockets of air keep you warm in winter?
options: Trapped air conducts thermal energy away from your body very rapidly.
Gases are very poor thermal conductors, making trapped air a good insulator.
Trapped air increases the mass of the jacket, producing its own heat.
Gases are excellent thermal conductors that attract heat from the environment.
